description.text: Virginio Vespignani was born in Rome on 12 February 1808 to a noble family, the youngest of five children of Count Giovan Francesco Vespignani and Maria Teresa Sarnani. From a young age he worked as a draughtsman, contributing illustrations to books that popularised Roman archaeology, including a collaboration with Luigi Rossini on a work about the Antiquities of Pompeii and later illustrations for Edward Dodwell’s treatise I sette colli di Roma (London, 1829). He trained under the neoclassical architect Luigi Poletti and, between 1837 and 1869, helped reconstruct the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls, continuing the work after Poletti’s death.

Vespignani became a favourite of Pope Pius IX, and the papal reign provided him with numerous commissions. He applied historical revival styles to projects such as the Church of the Madonna dell’Archetto (1851), the façade of Porta Pia (1852–68), and the restoration of the cemetery of Campo Verano, where he completed the first part of the “Pincetto” and the quadriportico in 1880. In addition to his religious and civic works, he designed the glass and cast‑iron Serra all’Orto Botanico (1855) and the opera houses of Orvieto (Teatro Mancinelli) and Viterbo (Teatro dell’Unione). He served as city architect of Rome, was a member of the pontifical commission on antiquities, and was President of the Accademia di San Luca; he was knighted in both the Order of St. Sylvester and the Order of Christ, and in 1855 the municipality of Rome awarded him a gold medal for his work during the third cholera pandemic.
